thread:
Aisha: Quick micro-pack of goal wording variants for different audiences (ICs, managers, execs). Want ultra-short, copy/paste-ready lines.
Tom: Love it. Can we include a "check" line for measurement and a one-line risk note?
Aisha: Yes. Format: 1) Goal (one line). 2) Measure -> target. 3) Risk (one line). 4) Ask (who/what we need).
Riley: IC growth example please.
Aisha: IC growth: 'Own rollout of streaming embeddings pipeline to cut embed latency and cost.' Measure-> 'p99 embedding latency down 50% vs baseline; cost per 1k embeds -20%.' Risk-> 'Data drift during A/B could skew evals.' Ask-> 'SRE time for infra tests + query logs access.'
Priya: Product example?
Aisha: Product: 'Increase multi-turn chat retention by improving context-window heuristics.' Measure-> '7-day retention for chat flows +8 percentage points.' Risk-> 'Edge cases increase hallucination.' Ask-> 'Eval set + user research time.'
Tom: Manager-friendly phrasing (for skip-levels): 'Led X to Y, moved Z by N, plan to scale via A.' Keep numbers.
Riley: Add a "tone-down" variant for external-facing summaries (customer emails, exec deck).
Aisha: External summary: 'Launched feature X that improved response relevance and reduced latency, resulting in better engagement and lower cost.' Keep it non-technical.
Priya: Self-review starter (compact): 'Delivered X -> outcome Y. Learned Z. Next: A.' Good for 1-2 lines.
Tom: Tiny manager prompts bank: 'What metric shows success?', 'What's the smallest deliverable that proves progress?', 'Who blocks us?', 'How should I update stakeholders and when?'.
People Ops Bot: Archive saved -> https://drive.redwood/goal-microcopy-pack (access: people-ops).
Aisha: I'll add these into the OKR template as alternate wording options and flag the examples in the handbook. Thanks!
Tom: I'll proof the external variant for clarity. :+1:
Riley: Will craft one more ops-focused example and ping here when done.
Aisha: Closing thread; final pack by EOD.
